title: Optimize THREE-base logical defect guards: save 2336 per direction (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Finite certificate and scoped integer-optimality proof for a new logical precision objective on David Ganz / Dugongue's [PR4510](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4510) rewritten THREE-base suffix ledger.

```diff
- Forward ADD/SCALE guards  (11,11): charge 191741
+ Forward ADD/SCALE guards  (11, 9): charge 189405
- Backward ADD/SCALE guards (13,13): charge 226707
+ Backward ADD/SCALE guards (13,11): charge 224371
```

Each direction saves 2336 under the declared charge `J=N_ADD*g_ADD+N_SCALE*g_SCALE`. Both allocations are uniquely optimal over nonnegative integer guards satisfying every published row inequality. The largest normalized output bounds are 7257/8192 and 827/1024. This is a logical defect-budget result on a historical word, with no claim of physical storage/runtime savings or new kappa.

The source ledger and its perturbation theorem are cited inputs, not re-audited deliverables. The new contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit David Ganz / Dugongue's PR4510 and PR4505, the borrowed-adapter/gauge/source-selector chain and the native/compiler predecessors retained in the package. The selected PR6030 frontier and every existing source are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Before: the uniform benchmark requires 11 forward or 13 backward guard bits under the predecessor's exact-input, exact-other-classes, logical-isometry model. After: SCALE needs two fewer bits at the unique event-weighted optimum.
- All 1264 output constraints pass, 632 per orientation. Monotonicity certificates prove optimality; a separately represented integer-arithmetic oracle enumerates all 1057 forward and 1457 backward integer pairs at or below the respective uniform charge. It finds the same unique optima.
- All 15 rejection controls pass normally and under optimization, including insufficient guards, a nonoptimal guard rejected by the optimality certificate, malformed guards and corrupt source bytes.
- CPython 3.12.15, standard library only: both direct warning-strict checks, both registered commands, metadata/source pins, committed bytes/modes and source ancestry pass at `bbf28e1a678e1a9cbc633f35de5231eaab967f01`. The two final separately timed registered commands take 0.051 s and 0.060 s locally, each below its 120 s timeout. These are validation durations, not a speed comparison.
- The official six-file export passes integrity and declared-input coverage; optimized replay with an empty executable PATH passes outside Git. The selected-baseline source-binding orientation passes after sparse inputs are materialized. No predecessor scientific replay is run.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/suffix-guard-allocation/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/suffix-guard-allocation/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/suffix-guard-allocation
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/suffix-guard-allocation --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Any CPython 3.12 executable can replace that path. The direct command prints `PASS_SUFFIX_GUARD_ALLOCATION` in a generated JSON receipt bound to the exact input and all five package files. Sparse checkouts must first materialize `research/native-suffix-errors`. Exact source pins, including the cited proof, are in SOURCES.json.

## Limitations

Optimality concerns the sufficient inequalities in the supplied ledger, not the smallest true error of the program. The charge sums additional logical defect guard bits over source-supplied event counts. It is not peak live storage, a physical mantissa prescription or a machine-cost theorem. Every non-ADD/SCALE class is exact under the explicitly inherited model.

Physical norm conversions, recursive defects/feedback, rounding-grid ownership, restoration and a complete paid implementation remain open. This historical allocation cannot be transferred to the selected PR6030 word without new source-bound weights. No selected framework assumption or complete multiplication theorem is discharged. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Selected cold replay, predecessor scientific suites, Lean and Docker were not run.

## Open next questions

Can a literal ADD/SCALE implementation realize these unequal entire-field tolerances with a smaller complete arithmetic bill? Start by translating its componentwise errors into the retained logical norm, then price width conversion, routing and restoration. Missing physical contracts are the blocker.

## Related open work

The live open-PR and Discussion search found no other contribution optimizing the PR4510 rewritten THREE-base ADD/SCALE event-weighted guard charge. PR4510 is a merged predecessor. [PR6119](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6119) is adjacent rounding work on the selected deferred-row interface; it studies suffix amplification of temporary-row noise, while this contribution allocates logical class tolerances on a different historical word. No same-instance numerical value is compared.

Completion refresh read the titles and bodies of all five other open account PRs created since the CLAIM: #6122, #6123, #6124, #6125 and #6126. They concern higher-rank query capacity, two-coset centre kernels, sampler-table sharing, direct-flow leaf tariffs and production Gaussian conditioning. None studies the PR4510 guard-allocation objective or reports a competing value for this instance. No extra numerical computations were run to compare them.

The [advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19241750) is the canonical investigation pointer. Main-tree formula/object searches, merged-PR searches, recent account work and current local claims were checked. Cached remote coverage includes 379 open PRs and 5775 Discussion records with complete pagination; sparse local coverage and unpublished work remain limitations.

## CI notes

CI is **uncertified** at commit `bbf28e1a678e1a9cbc633f35de5231eaab967f01`. In [run 40691885316](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40691885316), `plan` failed during Onboarding helper tests and the package replay was skipped. **The package replay did not run in CI.**

The failure is inherited from canonical main `721c03822c421b7f7fcbb2598993b947c4d88419`, the PR6030 admission commit whose subject contains `[skip ci]`, and is unrelated to this package. Its selected-record/documentation mismatch causes exactly these two test failures:

- `test_research_current_status.CurrentStatusTests.test_current_section_matches_selected_record` expects the exact marker `**0.003125804**` in `docs/research/current-status.md`. The document instead bolds `0.003125804 = 781451/250000000` together, so that marker is absent.
- `test_research_current_status.CurrentCiNavigationTests.test_current_ci_section_matches_selected_record` expects `make frontier6030-verify` in `docs/ci.md`, which still describes #5599 and `make frontier5599-verify`.

The log reports 678 onboarding tests, two failures and 23 skips. [PR6120's run 40691776027](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40691776027) fails the same two tests, confirmed from its failed-job log. No other onboarding failure is inferred from incidental diagnostic text.

All package checks listed above passed locally, but none was certified by this hosted run. **A maintainer must re-run CI after main's documentation is fixed.** No branch push, documentation fix or CI re-run was performed for this blocker.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: isolated.

Adds one standalone research package and its opt-in replay. No shared-code or selected-record changes.
